chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every oath that has an expiation (kaffarah), except for what is from divorce, or manumission, or a covenant, or a solemn pledge.'
ai.seo_question: Which types of oaths are exempt from the general rule of expiation (kaffarah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies that while most broken oaths require expiation, specific categories like divorce, manumission, and covenants are exempt because they carry distinct legal consequences in Islamic jurisprudence. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly approach to differentiating between general vows and those tied to specific acts of worship or legal transactions, ensuring that the expiation mechanism does not override the primary ruling of the act itself.
